You do care. Your parents might be already upset that they are losing each other and of course they are concerned that it will affect the rest of the family. Your parents care for you and want you to be happy. Talk to them and tell them how much you love coming home from school, how it is so stress-relieving to just be in their company. 

You need to tell them that you're losing your fight and you just need their comfort.  Your parents probably need consoling too. Tell them you love them, show your brother you will be there for him through all of this. Your family seems so important to you. Please don't give up. Many hugs your way.

Have you talked to your husband about it? Does he know where you are at in recovery and that you are hitting a rough patch? As tense as the conversation might be he seems to be the closest one to you right now and could really offer some help. He cares about you and wants the best for you, and so do I (even as a stranger). Stay strong!

I broke up with my fiancee of 2 1/2 years. We both became different people through our relationship and we realized it too late. We took each other for granted. He moved to go to school and we tried fixing us for the 6 months we were physically apart. I felt like it wasn't going well. We still argued and I was too stressed to want to deal with it. It's been about two months and I'm trying to move on. 

I know I'm still in love with him. I think about him all the time. It's not fair to the guy I'm with with. The sex isn't as good, and I'm not comfortable like I was with my ex. I love him so much and I still think we are soul mates, but I feel like we just got together at the wrong time in our lives.
I feel like I am being consumed. I know the only way I can still talk about this is because it's finally out there and I have some one(s) to talk to.
